claims.explanation: PCI-24781 is a hydroxamic-acid HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by lineage/transcriptional context rather than a single driver mutation: sensitive lines are enriched for RAS/RAF-pathway activation (BRAF/NRAS/KRAS mutations) and for loss of NF1, which together increase dependence on HDAC-mediated survival and DNA-repair signaling, while resistant lines are enriched for EGFR/MAP2K1-driven lung models and mesenchymal/osteosarcoma lines. HDAC inhibition reduces RAD51 and homologous recombination, so tumors with activated RAS/RAF or defective NF1 may be more vulnerable to the resulting replication/DNA-repair stress. The virtual-cell profile confirms the expected HDAC-inhibitor class response, supporting this as an on-target HDAC effect.

features.basis: NF1-mutant MPNSTs are highly sensitive to PCI-24781 (PMID 21084276); NF1 loss activates RAS signaling
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal/endometrial lines are enriched among sensitive lines; MAPK activation may increase HDAC dependence
NRAS-mutant melanoma/bladder lines appear among sensitive lines; RAS pathway activation
KRAS-mutant gastric lines are among sensitive lines, though KRAS also appears in resistant lines
PCI-24781 decreases RAD51 and inhibits homologous recombination; high RAD51 may buffer HDAC-inhibitor-induced DNA-repair defects
LSD1 inhibition sensitizes glioblastoma cells to HDAC inhibitors, implying LSD1 activity protects against HDAC inhibition
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1437, NCIH1650) are mostly in the least-affected group
MAP2K1-mutant NCIH1437 is among the least-affected lines
PCI-24781 induces ROS- and NF-kappaB-dependent apoptosis in lymphoma cells
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so p53 status alone is not selective; included as a weak negative feature
PCI-24781 is a broad HDAC inhibitor targeting HDAC1/2/3/6; higher target expression may increase sensitivity
PCI-24781 targets HDAC2; target expression may predict response
